Class 5 · Chapter 3 of 10

Fractions, mixed numbers and what is left

Connect pictures and quantities before solving repeated changes.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Solve stories with factors and multiples. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can match equivalent and mixed fractions.
  • I can order fractions and find a fraction of an amount.
  • I can find what is left after fraction changes.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 5

Mixed numbers

Each strip has 5 equal parts. One strip is full, the next has 4 shaded.

That is 1 whole and 4/5, written 1 4/5.

Count all the shaded parts: 9 fifths, so 1 4/5 = 9/5.

Screen 2 of 5

Equivalent fractions

Multiply the top and bottom by the same number.

5/7 = 10/14 because 5 × 2 = 10 and 7 × 2 = 14.

The shaded amount stays the same.

Screen 3 of 5

Put fractions in order

Give the fractions the same bottom number.

2/3 = 8/12, 3/4 = 9/12 and 5/6 = 10/12.

Now the order is easy: 2/3, then 3/4, then 5/6.

Screen 4 of 5

A fraction of an amount

To find 2/6 of 96, split 96 into 6 equal parts.

Each part is 96 ÷ 6 = 16.

2 parts make 32. So 2/6 of 96 is 32.

Screen 5 of 5

What is left after changes

A base has 42 crates. 1/6 are used, which is 7. That leaves 35.

Next 3/5 of the 35 are used, which is 21.

35 − 21 = 14 crates are left.

Words to know
mixed number
A whole number and a fraction together, like 1 4/5.
improper fraction
A fraction where the top is bigger than the bottom, like 9/5.
equivalent
Having the same value, like 5/7 and 10/14.

For parents

What your child learns

To find a fraction of an amount, divide by the denominator and multiply by the numerator. So 3/5 of 65 is 13 × 3 = 39. To compare unlike fractions, use a common denominator or a picture.

A common slip

Children often compare numerators or denominators alone. Use a common whole or common denominator, or test both fractions on equal strips.

5-minute home activity: Fraction strips

  1. Cut four equal paper strips.
  2. Fold them into halves, thirds, quarters and sixths.
  3. Place them side by side and order the fractions.
  4. Find 3/5 of 20 counters.
